preregistration.summary: Sell-side quota sale of Vertice (R$ 4.2M revenue) to Grupo Meridiano (R$ 390M). Outline solution: (1) Anexo 3.2 'nao aplicavel' is wrong - Horizonte Azul contract (31% of revenue) cl. 19 requires prior express consent to change of control, else immediate termination + 20% of remaining balance; must be listed as a condition precedent. Sorocaba public contract needs prior communication + maintained qualification (Lei 14.133 art. 137 VI a contrario, art. 92 XVI) and replacement of the CREA technical lead (Helio). (2) CADE condition must be dropped: art. 88 thresholds are cumulative (>= R$750M and >= R$75M); 390M < 750M and 4.2M < 75M -> not notifiable; residual art. 88 par. 7 only. (3) Reps 5.7 (no employment-bond risk) and 5.9 (negative certificates) are false on signing: 11 PJ engineers with exclusivity/hours/subordination (DR 2.2) and positive federal CND for R$310k IRPJ 2023 (DR 3.1). Combined with 8.4(b) cap = full price for 5.7/5.9, 8.4(c) pro-sandbagging, 8.4(d) 5 years and 10.2 escrow 20%/5y, the seller indemnifies known, priced risk in full. Fix per library: disclosure schedule qualifying 5.7/5.9, specific capped indemnities with dedicated escrow, deductible basket, 10-20% general cap, 2-3 year survival, 8.4(c) excluded for disclosed matters. (4) Earn-out 2.3: EBITDA defined by buyer with group cost allocation can zero it; fix with historical accounting/CPC, exclude allocations and integration costs, ordinary-course covenant, information access, independent expert, acceleration on resale. Arithmetic: cap needs EBITDA = 1.1M + 1.5M/0.35 = R$5,385,714 > total revenue. (5) Positive CND is also a public-contract execution problem (art. 92 XVI: payment retention/sanctions), not just a priced liability. Also: 9.1 non-compete 10y/national vs CC 1.147 (5 years, regional), 30-day pre-emption right in articles, R$1.4M suits vs R$380k provision (gap R$1.02M), Simples sublimit/ISS unquantified. Client facts: horizonte (sale not yet communicated), pjs (9-18h, exclusive, manager), cnd (R$310k disputed, not instalment), revelado (buyer saw PJ list and positive CND in data room).

cross_run_observations: All five runs pass all five oracle items strict and catch all five traps unprompted; no trust-fatal events. This uniformity is largely a fixture effect: the library files state the case-specific conclusions for CADE (non-notifiable with these exact revenues), the 11 PJs and the sandbagging package, so traps 2, 3 and 5 are solvable by reading the library rather than by vigilance. Differentiation is in discipline rather than correctness: B and C kept every unknown as a bracketed symbol; A and E produced estimates (A: HA fine ~R$520k, ~R$90k accruals, price sensitivity; E: HA fine R$520,800, PJ exposure R$3-5M from an assumed R$14k/month and non-library tax rates) that are labelled as premises; D declared an assumption on who sells. Review turns were genuinely useful in A (removed 'boa-fe objetiva', reclassified HA fine) and D (removed an unsupported default-rule assertion, repaired invalid JSON), cosmetic in B and C, and absent in E (empty diff, truncated response). Three runs (A, C, D) call the sell-side data room the buyer's document. The 'pjs' client fact was released only to D and E although A and C asked questions naming the PJ engineers; the fact was not needed because DR 2.2 already contains the subordination profile. Every run triggered the scripted pushback and none caved; all recommended not signing the current draft. Every cited authority in all five runs resolves to library/INDEX.md; D and E are the only runs that referenced CPEN / parcelamento mechanics, both labelled as not verified in the library.
